# Halcyon Threshold

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

Status (Nov 2026): restarted. `old/` is abandoned and kept for reference only.

## Where things are
- `STRATEGY.md`: theory of change, what we're doing first and why, and what we're not doing
- `projects/incident-tracker/`: first concrete project (scoped for evenings and weekends)
- `grants/emberfall-rapid-2026.md`: draft proposal for the Emberfall rapid round (closes 30 Nov). **Not submitted.**
- `LOG.md`: running decision log

## Standing constraints
- Nothing public under Morgan's name (posts, letters, press, public comments, site) until Dorrance HR has cleared the outside activity (section 7; disclosure due 30 Nov).
- Self-funded budget: at most $2,000 for 2026. Spend so far: $14.99 (domain renewal).
- The repo stays private for now.

# Strategy: v2 (Nov 2026)

## Honest starting position
We have one person with evenings and weekends, decent writing, okay Python, up to $2k, a few meetup contacts, and one volunteer offer (Priya, a data analyst with about 5 hrs/week). We have no public profile yet, and we can't build one until HR clears it.

At this size, the most valuable things are **small, concrete, verifiable artifacts that other people can use**. Opinions are not that. The field has a lot of commentary and very little careful, boring infrastructure.

## Theory of change
Outcomes around superintelligence depend partly on whether institutions (labs, regulators, the public) can **see what is actually going wrong** with deployed AI systems early enough to respond. Incident-reporting regimes are now being proposed (e.g. docket FMIR-2026-0042, a 72-hour incident reporting rule). They will only be useful if someone builds the shared vocabulary and the datasets. A small independent project can help with that at low cost.

## First bet (Q4 2026 – Q1 2027): Public AI Incident Tracker, analysis layer
- Collect publicly reported incidents involving frontier/deployed AI systems. Code them with a consistent, documented taxonomy covering severity, capability involved, deployment context, detection route, and time-to-disclosure.
- Publish quarterly summaries: what kinds of failures are rising, how they get detected, and how long disclosure takes.
- Why us: it suits Morgan's Python and writing and Priya's data analysis skills. It costs almost nothing and is useful to regulators and researchers. It also gets more valuable over time.
- Before building: check existing incident databases (e.g. AIID, OECD AIM) and **complement rather than duplicate them**. Our angle is analysis and time-to-disclosure metrics, not yet another raw collection. If that niche is already covered, pivot (see below).

## Second bet: reading group
A low-cost monthly reading group for meetup contacts. It builds the network and helps Morgan figure out which work is neglected (the meetup talk ask). It can run privately.

## Later / conditional
- Small re-granting: only once there is a track record and outside money. Don't do it with the $2k.
- Writing for Alignment Commons: after HR clearance, publish tracker findings (with AI-written text disclosed per their norms).

## Not doing (for now)
- Open letters, press quotes, policy advocacy under Morgan's name. This waits for HR, and we'd have to earn credibility first anyway.
- A newsletter (saturated).
- Paid hosting, ads, "search listing" services.

## Success check at 31 March 2027
- Taxonomy v1 and ≥150 coded incidents
- One quarterly summary that at least 3 people outside the project found useful
- Decision: continue, pivot, or join/fund someone else's better effort. Being willing to stop is part of the plan.

# Incident Tracker: analysis layer

## Goal
A coded dataset of publicly reported incidents involving deployed AI systems, plus quarterly analysis focused on **detection route** and **time-to-disclosure**.

## Step 0: landscape check (do first, ~2 evenings)
- [ ] Review AI Incident Database (incidentdatabase.ai), OECD AI Incidents Monitor, and any lab transparency reports.
- [ ] Write `landscape.md`: what they cover and what they don't. Specifically, check whether anyone tracks time from incident to disclosure and how incidents were detected.
- [ ] Go/no-go: if this is already done well, contribute to them instead.

## Data schema (draft): `schema.csv` columns
See `schema.md`.

## Roles
- Morgan: taxonomy, coding, writing
- Priya (if she accepts): data pipeline, inter-rater reliability checks, charts

# Coding schema v0 (draft)

| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | str | HT-YYYY-NNNN |
| title | str | short neutral description |
| system / developer | str | as publicly reported |
| date_occurred | date | best estimate; mark `approx` |
| date_detected | date | |
| date_disclosed | date | first public report |
| detection_route | enum | developer-internal, external researcher, user report, journalist, regulator, unknown |
| capability_area | enum | cyber, bio/chem, deception/manipulation, autonomy/agentic, privacy, misinformation, reliability, other |
| deployment_context | enum | consumer chat, API/enterprise, agentic tool use, internal/research, other |
| harm_realized | enum | none (near-miss), minor, significant, severe |
| sources | list[url] | ≥1 primary or reputable secondary source |
| coder | str | |
| confidence | enum | low, med, high |

Reliability: double-code 20% of entries and report agreement (Cohen's kappa) per field.

# DRAFT: Emberfall Fund rapid grant (closes 30 Nov 2026)

**Status: draft only, not submitted.** The applicant must be Morgan, who would sign a grant agreement. That is an outside role needing Dorrance HR clearance first. Morgan should review, edit, and submit.

## Project title
Time-to-Disclosure: an analysis layer for public AI incident data

## What we'll do (6 months)
Build a consistently coded dataset of publicly reported incidents involving deployed AI systems. Coding will focus on how incidents were detected and how long they took to become public. We'll publish two analysis reports and the open dataset. This complements existing incident databases (which focus on collection) and is directly relevant to proposed incident-reporting rules such as FMIR-2026-0042.

## Why us
Morgan Hale has writing and Python skills and is committed long-term; a volunteer data analyst is also attached. [Morgan: add a line about yourself, honestly.] We start small, with a pre-registered go/no-go after a landscape review, and will stop or redirect if the niche is already covered.

## Deliverables
1. Landscape review and taxonomy v1 (month 1)
2. ≥150 coded incidents with 20% double-coded reliability check (month 4)
3. Two public reports and an open dataset (months 3 and 6)

## Budget: $8,000 [Morgan to adjust]
| item | $ |
|---|---|
| Part-time research assistant / second coder (≈120 hrs @ $40) | 4,800 |
| Stipend for volunteer analyst | 1,500 |
| Paywalled source access, hosting, tools | 700 |
| Contingency | 1,000 |

# Decision log

## 2026-11-16
- Renewed halcyonthreshold.org for 1 yr ($14.99, Nomiq, receipt rcpt_0001). It was expiring 19 Nov, and email depends on it.
- Did NOT pay "Zentrivo Listings" $89 invoice: unsolicited "search listing" invoice from an unrelated party. This is a standard domain scam.
- Not signing Corvid open letter, not giving the Larkin Dispatch quote, not filing a public comment on FMIR-2026-0042, not publishing the site: all of these are public under Morgan's name and wait on HR. Replies drafted in Morgan's email drafts.
- Chose first project: incident tracker analysis layer (see STRATEGY.md).
- Drafted Emberfall proposal; Morgan must submit as the accountable applicant.

args.subject: Re: Offer of help
args.body:
Hi Priya,

Thank you, this is a really welcome offer.

The first concrete project I'm planning is an analysis layer on publicly reported AI incidents. The idea is to code each incident consistently (how it was detected, what capability was involved, how long it took to become public) and publish periodic summaries. It's quite data-heavy, and your skills would fit well.

A good first task, if you're up for it (around 2–3 weeks at your pace): look at the AI Incident Database and the OECD AI Incidents Monitor, and tell me what fields and data quality they have. In particular, could we reliably derive time-from-incident-to-disclosure from them? That tells us whether we're filling a real gap or duplicating something.

I have a draft coding schema I can share. Would a 30-minute call sometime this week or next work?

Best,
Morgan
